title: CPP Minister Clarifies RP14 Million Subsidized Housing Salary Requirement
text:
Is there confusion surrounding subsidized housing in Indonesia? This article clarifies recent developments in the country’s housing policy , specifically addressing income requirements for low-income individuals. Learn about the current regulations, proposed adjustments, and ongoing discussions surrounding the subsidized housing program.
Housing Minister Clarifies Subsidized Housing Policy Amidst Public Debate Jakarta – Recent discussions surrounding IndonesiaS subsidized housing policy have prompted Minister of Housing and Settlement Areas (PKP), Maruarar Sirait , to address public concerns and clarify the government’s intentions.
Published: October 26, 2023
Understanding the Income Threshold Confusion arose following reports suggesting a minimum salary requirement of Rp14 million (approximately $875 USD) to qualify for subsidized housing. Minister Sirait, also known as Ara, emphasized that this figure represents the limit of income, not a minimum requirement.
The minister addressed the misunderstanding directly, stating:
Just the limit of income.So, what you understand is, people who earn Rp. 14 million can only buy MBR houses, or up to Rp. 14 million that can be? Does that mean my policy is prorakyat or not?
Maruarar Sirait, Minister of Housing and Settlement Areas (PKP)
This clarification is crucial for prospective homeowners who may have been deterred by the misconstrued facts.
The Target Demographic: Low-Income Individuals The core objective of the subsidized housing program remains focused on providing affordable housing for low-income individuals, categorized as Masyarakat Berpenghasilan Rendah (MBR). Current regulations define MBR as individuals earning a maximum of Rp7 million per month if single, or Rp8 million per month if married.
Key Points: Current MBR Income Limits Single individuals: Maximum Rp7 million/month Married individuals: Maximum Rp8 million/month Proposed Adjustments to income Limits Minister Sirait has voiced concerns that the existing income limits are too restrictive, particularly for families. He argues that the current thresholds do not adequately reflect the financial realities of families with dependents.
he elaborated on the rationale behind the proposed changes:
If Rp. 7 million,have one wife,two children,how much do you want? We will increase it,so that the opportunity to get more MBR houses.
Maruarar Sirait, Minister of Housing and Settlement Areas (PKP)
The proposed increase aims to broaden access to subsidized housing for families who are currently excluded due to the low-income ceiling.
Ongoing Review and Legal Considerations The proposal to raise the MBR salary limits is currently under review. Minister Sirait indicated that he would be consulting with Minister of Law supratman Andi Agtas to discuss the necessary revisions to existing regulations.
This collaborative effort underscores the government’s commitment to refining the subsidized housing policy to better serve the needs of its citizens.
Social Media Reaction and Public Perception The initial announcement regarding the Rp14 million figure sparked considerable debate on social media platforms. Many citizens expressed concern that the policy would primarily benefit higher-income individuals, contrary to the program’s intended purpose.
The minister’s subsequent clarification seeks to address these concerns and reassure the public that the subsidized housing program remains focused on assisting low-income families.
